principles: Read legacy inputs before switching canonical writes so existing evidence chains remain valid.
Centralize canonical role, schema, marker, and package facts at testable choke points to prevent string drift.
Verify every external boundary for new behavior, legacy-input compatibility, and error or one-shot behavior.
Commit only Story-scoped files and preserve other developers dirty worktrees.
drivers: Historical artifact and signature freshness must remain compatible with already-installed projects.
Review, init, quorum, and pre-push gates must not silently fail during the naming migration.
Package and lockfile metadata, bins, and dependency references must move as one installable registry identity.

options.name: A: canonical-write dual-read migration
pros: Meets the current proof-or-stop identity goals in CHK-001 through CHK-007.
Historical role, marker, schema, and approval inputs remain readable.
Central aliases and boundary tests constrain the compatibility surface.
cons: Touches multiple gate and package boundaries and requires full regression.
Existing package or bin callers may need an explicit migration strategy.

options.name: B: leave package/bin and schemas frozen
pros: Smaller change with short-term compatibility for old installations.
cons: Directly violates CHK-003 through CHK-007 and the requested migration.
Future proof-or-stop writes would continue producing lattice identity residue.
The user-visible rename would remain incomplete.

rationale: Option A is selected because this Story explicitly requires the remaining package, schema, marker, role, and bin residue to migrate to canonical identities; compatibility is retained only at legacy-input and historical-read boundaries.

preMortem.scenario: A new remote approval uses the proof-or-stop schema while the hook still accepts only the lattice schema.
preMortem.trigger: pre-push reports an invalid approval schema after release_approve_push.
preMortem.consequence: A valid main release is blocked.
preMortem.mitigation: Share schema aliases across the writer, CLI reader, and hook, and test new and legacy schemas plus one-shot consumption.

preMortem.scenario: Role canonicalization changes only the registry while review_run or quorum still hard-codes the lattice prefix.
preMortem.trigger: After a new proof-or-stop reviewer run or pass is written, reviewer_list or the gate cannot see the lane.
preMortem.consequence: Review evidence is treated as missing or excluded from quorum.
preMortem.mitigation: Use one role alias and normalization helper across review-run, finding/pass, init-check, quorum, and prompt dispatch, with new and legacy input tests.

preMortem.scenario: The marker writer is renamed but the reader no longer recognizes an installed lattice block.
preMortem.trigger: init --upgrade appends a duplicate managed block to an old CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.
preMortem.consequence: The user project contains duplicate or orphaned configuration.
preMortem.mitigation: Use a dual-read boundary test that updates an old block in place and writes only proof-or-stop markers in new files.

preMortem.scenario: Root and sibling package metadata, lockfiles, or in-repository dependencies become inconsistent.
preMortem.trigger: npm install, npm pkg get name, or the global lab entrypoint fails.
preMortem.consequence: The package cannot resolve or its self-host gate silently fails.
preMortem.mitigation: Synchronize all package metadata, lockfiles, and imports, then run package identity, build, install, and pre-push detection tests.
